coverage_limits: The allowed target record excludes the target court's final reasoning and outcome. No use or alignment review may infer that section 14(1)(b) was or was not ultimately satisfied, and no section 18 post-order status may be inferred.

The 1 January 1973 notification and its governing statutory basis are not supplied. The record supports a witness allegation that the New Zealand Insurance company stood transferred to and vested in respondent No.1, but it does not independently supply the legal instrument or establish a transfer of the tenancy interest.

The exact legally relevant date and character of M.L. Sharma's occupation relative to 9 June 1952 remain unresolved. The supplied material says employment/accommodation 'since 1952' or permitted use 'even before 1972' but does not fix a qualifying transfer or subletting date.

No fixed written-consent document, prescribed section 17 sub-tenancy notice, or complete 1940 lease instrument is supplied. The landlord witness also stated that he did not know whether a written tenancy document was executed.

The fixed graph omits some supplied testimony and exhibit descriptions, including RW2 employment-related records at L143-L144 and RW3 testimony at L150-L155. This review does not add or rewrite graph facts from those passages; it uses them only where a proposed authority-use reason itself cited or depended on the allowed source.

Several authorities arise under other jurisdictions or statutes, including Andhra Pradesh, Bombay/Maharashtra, Goa, the earlier Delhi and Ajmer Act, and banking statutes. Their usefulness is limited to the specific analogy or contrast stated; no identity of statutory mechanism is inferred.

Several authority texts are partial, reported through another case, OCR-preserved, or supplied with historically unverified statutory-version status. Exact supplied wording is preserved, and no outside correction, later-law audit, or historical consolidation is imported.
